evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry reproduces the Shuowen explanation of 書 as 箸也, 从聿，者聲, glossed in the entry as writing/setting down: 聿 is the semantic element and 者 the phonetic element in this traditional analysis. It lists senses separately: write, record, writing/text, book, letter, document, script style and calligraphy. The list is not a chronology and does not establish when each sense arose.
evidence.title: [A01835] 書 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: Describes traditional 書 as a phonosemantic compound, with 聿 as meaning component and 者 as sound component. It reports modern readings yù and zhě for the components and gives Baxter–Sagart-style comparisons for 書 and 者, while its cited character page does not provide independently inspected original-object evidence for 聿 or a dated derivation. The source says the sounds were more similar in older Chinese. This is a secondary account; it does not override the locally supplied Baxter–Sagart row for 書 or establish the corresponding 者 row.

gaps: The original earliest attestation and dated development sequence of 書 remain unestablished. The accessible official variant dictionary reports several paleographic source tables as unavailable; do not infer dates from general script chronology or the modern label on a redraw.

The Shuowen account supports 聿 as semantic and 者 as phonetic within that lexicographic analysis. The local Baxter–Sagart table has 書 MC syo, OC *s-ta, gloss “write” (sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, 書 row), but no checked local row for 者 was supplied. Dong Chinese gives secondary comparative reconstructions, but the original-object name/pronunciation of 聿 is not independently established here.

The semantic connection from writing/recording to text, book, letter and document cannot be ordered chronologically from the dictionary's gloss sequence. The page cites old-text examples, but the inspected sources do not settle the dates of composition or manuscript witnesses for each use.

Local Unihan rows supplied for 書 and 书 both give kMandarin shū (sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt, respective character rows). Both exact Unicode character lookup URLs were attempted but unavailable through the browser, so no official character-specific click-through source was verified.

The Commons bronze redraw is explicitly marked as needing a time period; the seal redraw represents a Shuowen seal style. Neither is an ancient artifact photograph or independent paleographic dating evidence. The seal original SVG was inaccessible to the browser although its description page and exact direct URL were verified.

No queried Xiaoxuetang glyph candidate was supplied, and no character-specific Xiaoxuetang record was retrieved, so none is selected. No local bulk extract is recommended: source reuse terms and a clear repeatability benefit were not both established.
